title: WHAT HAPPENED?
sub: Archaeologists mapped Greater Angkor as one of the largest urban complexes of the pre-industrial world. Over time, power shifted away from it. When and why are still debated.
say: Archaeologists mapped Greater Ang-kor as one of the largest urban complexes of the pre-industrial world. Over time, power shifted away from it. When and why are still debated.

title: THEORY 1: WAR
sub: Later accounts link Angkor's decline to attacks by the Siamese kingdom of Ayutthaya. The year 1431 is the conventional date, and it is disputed.
say: Later accounts link Ang-kor's decline to attacks by the Siamese kingdom of Ah-yoot-tah-yah. The year fourteen thirty-one is the conventional date, and it is disputed.

title: THEORY 2: CLIMATE
sub: Tree rings from Vietnam show decades-long droughts in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, broken by intense monsoons. The researchers call climate a contributing factor, not the only cause.
say: Tree rings from Vietnam show decades-long droughts in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, broken by intense monsoons. The researchers call climate a contributing factor, not the only cause.

title: THEORY 3: WATER
sub: Angkor depended on a huge network of canals and reservoirs. Some researchers argue that droughts strained water supplies, while extreme floods damaged parts of the network.
say: Ang-kor depended on a huge network of canals and reservoirs. Some researchers argue that droughts strained water supplies, while extreme floods damaged parts of the network.

title: THEORY 4: TRADE
sub: Some researchers suggest that access to sea trade may have influenced the later shift of power south, toward the Mekong.
say: Some researchers suggest that access to sea trade may have influenced the later shift of power south, toward the May-kong.

title: SLOW, NOT SUDDEN
sub: In 2019, scientists studied mud cores from the moat of Angkor Thom. Signs of burning, forest clearing and soil erosion were already declining in the fourteenth century, before the conventional date of 1431.
say: In twenty nineteen, scientists studied mud cores from the moat of Ang-kor Tom. Signs of burning, forest clearing and soil erosion were already declining in the fourteenth century, before the conventional date of fourteen thirty-one.

title: NEVER EMPTY
sub: And Angkor Wat was never completely abandoned. It stayed in use as a Buddhist site, and it still is today.
say: And Ang-kor Wat was never completely abandoned. It stayed in use as a Buddhist site, and it still is today.

title: ALL OF THE ABOVE?
sub: The evidence points to a complex, gradual decline. No single explanation is established.
say: The evidence points to a complex, gradual decline. No single explanation is established.
